newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to negotiate new ESAF in 1997/98 - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to negotiate new ESAF in 1997/98 - IMF.

text.p: Pakistan is likely to negotiate a new structural adjustment loan with the International Monetary Fund in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June), an IMF official said on Thursday.

"If eveything goes well, if performance is satisfactory, then our expectation is that Pakistan in the next fiscal year will go back to the ESAF arrangement," IMF Middle East department chief Antonio Furtado told a news conference.
A visiting IMF mission said on Wednesday it had approved Pakistan's latest stabilisation package and would recommend reactivation of a stalled $600 million standby loan.
"These policies under the standby are unusual in the sense that they include a lot of structural reforms already," Furtado said. "This arrangement, standby, is a bridge to resuming ESAF."

Pakistan concluded a three-year $1.5-billion enhanced structural adjustment facility with the IMF that began in February 1994, but payments were suspended a year later because Islamabad failed to achieve agreed targets.
